content.title: Miami loses to Purdue, misses NCAA tournament Sweet 16. See highlights
content.text: Updated March 22, 2026, 6:20 p.m. ETMiami basketball takes on the preseason No. 1 team in the country when it tips off against Purdue in the 2026 NCAA tournament second round. The winner moves on to the Sweet 16 in San Jose against No. 3-seeded Gonzaga/No. 11-seeded Texas.The seventh-seeded Hurricanes (26-8) opened their March Madness with an 80-66 win against Missouri. One more victory would not only bust several brackets, but it would give first-year coach Jai Lucas an NCAA Division I-record 20-game turnaround from last season. The No. 2 Boilermakers (28-8) have won five straight after a 104-71 walloping of Queens and a Big Ten tournament title despite losing four of six to close the regular season. Matt Painter seeks his ninth Sweet 16 appearance in 21 years as head coach.Miami's two top players have experience against Purdue, with Malik Reneau transferring in from Indiana and Tre Donaldson playing last year at Michigan. They'll look to contain a balanced and dynamic Boilermaker offense led by consensus All-America guard Braden Smith, backcourt mate Fletcher Loyer and multi-talented big men Trey Kaufman-Renn and Oscar Cluff.Watch Miami vs. Purdue live on Fubo (free trial)The Palm Beach Post will be providing live score and game updates through the final buzzer. Follow along below.Miami vs Purdue score updates in NCAA tournament bracketThis section will be updated when the game begins.TEAMSFIRST HALFSECOND HALFSCOREMiami402969Purdue384179 Miami basketball season ends with loss to Purdue in NCAA tournamentA hard-fought goes in Purdue's favor, as Miami fell short, 79-69, in the second round of the 2026 NCAA tournament in St. Louis on Sunday. Fletcher Loyer scored 24 points on 6-for-7 shooting (4-for-4 on 3-pointers) and 8-for-8 from the free-throw line. Shelton Henderson had 18 points and eight rebounds for Miami (26-8). Purdue in control late in second halfThe Hurricanes are running out of time to make the Sweet 16. Purdue's offense continues to hum, shooting 56% from the field and holding a 72-65 lead with 2:48 remaining. Miami starting to slip as Purdue keeps up hot shootingThe Hurricanes find themselves down eight with 8:50 to play, thanks in large part to Trey Kaufman-Renn's 16 points and Fletcher Loyer's 18 points and 4-for-4 from the 3-point line. As a team, Purdue is shooting 55% (20-for-40) and Miami is only 46% (22-for-48) from the field. Purdue jumps back in front to start second halfA 12-5 spurt to start the second half put the Boilermakers ahead, 50-45, but the Hurricanes seemed to settle down after the run. This driving Shelton Henderson bucket cut the Miami deficit to three. C.J. Cox suffers injury; Purdue guard goes back to locker roomThere has not yet been an update provided on C.J. Cox, the Purdue guard who seemed to suffer a right knee injury during the second half of the NCAA tournament game against Miami.CBS sideline reporter Jon Rothstein reported minutes later that Cox is questionable to return to the game. Cox is reportedly trying to test his leg to see if he can make a return.With 17:04 to play in the second half, Cox on was on a fast break with the basketball and has he went up for the layup, his right knee seemed to buckle as he was going up against a pair of Hurricanes. Offensive flurry, capped by Tre Donaldson, gives Miami the lead at halftimePurdue took a momentary lead on three straight 3-pointers from Purdue's C.J. Cox, but Tre Donaldson's driving layup with just about two seconds left in the half gave Miami a 40-38 halftime advantage. Both teams are shooting over 50% from the field, but the Hurricanes have a slight 15-13 rebounding advantage. Miami flexing its muscle inside, taking the lead over PurdueThe Hurricanes have stiffened their defense, forcing seven turnovers, and have allowed their scoring to come from the inside, then out. Shelton Henderson's early 10 points have helped push the Hurricanes ahead late in the first half. Miami getting beat up inside by Purdue's big manThe Hurricanes seem to be settling in, but Purdue center Trey Kaufman-Renn already had 10 points on 5 of 7 shooting and five rebounds as the Boilermakers hold on to a small lead. Miami cools off, Purdue does notAfter opening the game 4-for-8 from the field, the Hurricanes missed four of their next five shots. Meanwhile, Purdue went on a 13-2 run, which including a pair of Fletcher Loyer 3-pointers to give Purdue a seven-point lead. Miami, Purdue opening up the offense in early goingThe first play of the game brought the St. Louis crowd out of their seats before they could even settle in. Miami's Tre Donaldson found Ernest Udeh Jr. on an alley-oop off the opening tip, and the Hurricanes took a slim two-point lead into the first timeout. Both teams are shooting well to start -- Miami is at 50% and Purdue is at 67%. Miami vs Purdue basketball historyThe Hurricanes are 1-3 in four previous games against the Boilermakers. Miami won the most recent matchup, a 58-54 victory on Dec. 8, 2020 in Coral Gables as part of the ACC/Big Ten Challenge. UM rallied from 18 points behind at halftime to win.
